newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BASKET DEALS, YEN DOMINATE BUDAPEST FOREX FUTURES.
newsitem.headline: BASKET DEALS, YEN DOMINATE BUDAPEST FOREX FUTURES.

text.p: Dollar and mark basket deals, especially for December, and the Japanese yen accounted for most turnover on Budapest's currency futures markets on Monday.

The mark and dollar, which make up 70 percent and 30 percent respectively of the central bank basket against which the forint floats, took up one third of the modest 2.47 billion forints turnover on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) and all trade on the smaller Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE).
The yen, which is not traded on the BSE, accounted for most of the rest of BCE trade.
"Due to the impact of (Friday's) repo cuts, market interest rates are expected to drop and this favours basket sellings." said Janos Fonyodi of Termin broker
The dollar dropped 80 fillers for December to 197.20 forints due to its easing on the spot market. December mark closed at 116.30, unchanged.
The yen soared for all maturities by between 5.25 and 6.9 forints per 100 units on expectations of future rises against the dollar, dealers said.
"The yen is expected to firm substantially in the dollar cross," Fonyodi said, adding that Japan's surplus in trade with the U.S. is expected to rise substantially.
The BSE saw turnover 705 million forints, split between dollar/mark basket deals for June and December.
The June and December mark rose 0.31 and 0.42 to 107.57 and 116.26 fprints respectively while the June and December dollar fell 1.12 and 2.00 to 195.00 and 199.3.
